server name = Keycloak client id = resource_access key
ALSO IN THE REALM — NOT MCP PERMISSIONS
openshell-user — OpenShell gateway login. Held by all
three bankers. Grants no MCP tool access by itself.
openshell-onboarding-svc. Also no MCP tool roles.
composite · 1 client role, and is itself
the realm role the Envoy gate wants
list the banker's assigned clients with AUM & risk
top client by assets under management
search market news by semantic relevance
risk profile + KYC status for a client
calculate tax for a given income
HOW TO READ THIS — a call to tool T on server S succeeds only if the caller's access token clears BOTH gates
Gate 1 — Envoy sidecar on each MCP server pod: verifies the JWT against Keycloak's JWKS, then requires that realm_access.roles contains the card's role (grey line). Server-level, not per-tool.
Gate 2 — MCP Gateway AuthPolicy (Authorino CEL, tool-access-check): requires resource_access["S"].roles to contain tool:T, keyed by the x-mcp-servername header. Per-tool.
Keycloak composite roles are what emit both claim shapes from one grant: holding banker alone clears Gate 1 and Gate 2 for all four servers above the divider.
So: alice can run all 11 tools. bob and charlie can run the 10 above the divider — calc_tax gets them a 403 from Gate 2 (and never reaches the pod, Gate 1 rejects it too).
